concepts.concept: A solemn portrait at a fictional ceremonial inspection desk. The subject presents an upright commendation sheet whose writing is being covered by broad, freshly applied black redaction bars; a little blank medal and her carefully held expression turn the official honor into an absurd loss of voice.
concepts.benefit: Face, page, stamp hand and visible ink state can occupy one shallow plane, making the bureaucratic contradiction readable.
concepts.risk: Tiny print cannot carry the satire; broad black bars and an empty medal need enough projected area.

concepts.concept: A fictional award portrait in a modest parade room. The subject solemnly accepts a tiny ceremonial ribbon attached to a large blank placard held at chest height while a clerk measures its emptiness with a ruler, giving absence the seriousness of an achievement.
concepts.benefit: Person-centered absurd precision; an empty placard can dominate the lower half without hiding the face.
concepts.risk: A blank field alone may read as an unfinished advertisement; the measuring action must be visible and directed.

concepts.concept: A fictional ceremonial inspection portrait. The subject stands before a desk holding one palm-sized paper flower upright while an official carefully stamps the flower pot; a row of identical pots waits like applicants, turning a simple personal offering into an institutional ritual.
concepts.benefit: A distinct human presence and a modest, legible act can coexist; repeated pending objects establish the procedural context.
concepts.risk: Flower stamping is absurd but may lack enough culturally specific satirical force without later compatible retrieval.
